task: Comprehensive gap identification, classification, and priority ranking across all six dimensions

content_gaps.gap: Zero Very Difficult items (0% vs CAQS 10% target)
content_gaps.severity_rationale: VDiff items test advanced competence and professional judgment. Complete absence means practice sessions cannot prepare candidates for the hardest exam questions.
content_gaps.reason_cannot_recalibrate: No existing item base to draw from. VDiff items require multi-step analysis, judgment under uncertainty, and synthesis across topics — definition-match items cannot be recalibrated to VDiff.

content_gaps.gap: Difficult items 85 current vs 635 target (13.4% of target)
content_gaps.severity_rationale: Difficult items form the backbone of exam discrimination. A 550-item shortfall means practice sessions disproportionately test at low-to-moderate demand.

split_estimate.from_recalibration: ~200-300 items currently labeled Moderate that genuinely test at Difficult cognitive demand (post-DL-031 reclassification)
split_estimate.from_new_content: ~250-350 new items needed even after recalibration

content_gaps.blocker: DL-031 must be resolved first — current Moderate pool likely inflated by ~800-1000 Easy items. True recalibration surface only knowable after DL-031 fix.

content_gaps.gap: Zero Evaluate items (0% vs CAQS 15% target)
content_gaps.severity_rationale: Evaluate = professional judgment, recommendation, and decision-making. These are the highest-value skills tested on the CMA exam. Complete absence means candidates never practice evaluative reasoning.
content_gaps.reason_cannot_recalibrate: Evaluate items require scenario-based professional judgment (compare alternatives, make recommendations, assess trade-offs). Definition-match or calculation-only items cannot be recalibrated upward to Evaluate. Every Evaluate item must be newly authored.

content_gaps.gap: Analyze items 10 current vs 635 target (1.6% of target)
content_gaps.severity_rationale: Analyze covers data interpretation, variance analysis, trend identification — core management accounting activities. Severe under-representation distorts practice session realism.

split_estimate.from_recalibration: ~150-250 items currently labeled Apply/Understand that genuinely test at Analyze level (multi-step reasoning from exhibits, pattern identification)

content_gaps.note: Some Analyze items can be created by adding exhibit-dependency to existing Apply-level calculation items (same numbers, require extraction from exhibits rather than direct fact-pattern). This reduces the pure-new-content burden.

content_gaps.gap: Under-coverage of ASC 842 (leases), ASC 740 (income taxes), ASC 805 (business combinations)
content_gaps.severity_rationale: These are tested on the CMA Part 1 exam and represent high-weight topics within Section A. Under-coverage creates blueprint alignment risk.
sub_topics: ASC 842: Lessee operating vs. finance lease classification and measurement
ASC 740: Deferred tax assets/liabilities, valuation allowance, effective tax rate reconciliation
ASC 805: Acquisition method, goodwill calculation, bargain purchase
content_gaps.target_blooms: Mix of Apply (calculations) and Analyze (interpretation), minimum 2 Evaluate items per topic

content_gaps.gap: Predictive/prescriptive analytics depth, blockchain applications, AI governance, robotic process automation
content_gaps.severity_rationale: Section F is the fastest-evolving CMA domain. Current items appear definitional only. Candidates need application-level items for analytics methods and evaluative items for technology selection decisions.
sub_topics: Predictive analytics: regression interpretation, time-series forecasting, classification models
Prescriptive analytics: optimization, simulation, decision trees
Blockchain: triple-entry accounting, smart contract audit implications
AI governance: model risk management, bias detection, explainability requirements
RPA: process selection criteria, control implications, exception handling
content_gaps.target_blooms: Mix of Apply (tool selection, method application), Analyze (output interpretation), and Evaluate (technology adoption recommendations)

content_gaps.gap: COSO ERM items test framework recall but not application to risk-response decisions
content_gaps.severity_rationale: The CMA exam tests ERM application (selecting appropriate risk responses, integrating ERM with strategy), not just framework memorization. Current items likely definitional.
sub_topics: Risk appetite vs. risk tolerance scenario application
Risk response selection (avoid/accept/reduce/share) for given business scenarios
Entity-level vs. process-level risk assessment differentiation
content_gaps.target_blooms: Minimum 5 Evaluate items for risk-response selection scenarios

content_gaps.gap: 60 cases (~330 items) lack full certification across scored_cases2-5
content_gaps.severity_rationale: Case studies test integrated reasoning — the highest-value CMA preparation format. Uncertified cases cannot enter the learner delivery pool.
content_gaps.note: Case certification requires 6-dimension AI verification per CAQS §1.6 plus exhibit data-consistency verification. Higher per-item effort than standalone MCQ certification.
blockers: DL-032 (uniform difficulty labeling must be resolved before or during certification)

quality_gaps.gap: 95 Certified Pack E Section C items have structurally absent distractor ExplanationWrong fields (3 per item = 285 fields)
quality_gaps.severity_rationale: Learners see zero educational feedback on incorrect choices for 95 Certified items in the active delivery pool. High learner-safety impact.
quality_gaps.authoring_target_per_field: ≥50 chars, choice-specific, references accounting principle, explains misconception
quality_gaps.status: Open — scoped, authoring not yet executed

quality_gaps.gap: Metadata-block ChoiceA-D shift causing wrong-topic distractor ExplanationWrong text on 58 Certified items (Pack A Section E)
quality_gaps.severity_rationale: Learners who select wrong answers see feedback about a completely different topic. Active learner-safety risk — misleading educational feedback on Certified items.
quality_gaps.fields_to_author: ~171 ExplanationWrong fields require choice-specific, topic-accurate distractor text
quality_gaps.root_cause: Dual-block architecture: metadata block stores stale template choices from rotation group; content block (rendered to learner) has correct choices. ExplanationWrong fields are indexed to metadata choices, producing wrong-topic text.
quality_gaps.methodology_note: Must use within-object extraction (not forward-scan regex) to avoid DL-029 false positives. Content-block Choices.A-D is the authoritative source of truth.
quality_gaps.status: Resolved for Section E items per DL-016 entry (S805, 2026-07-26). Confirm scope: remaining items in Sections A/D of Pack A/C/D with dual-block architecture.
quality_gaps.verification_action: Re-confirm current DL-016 scope across Packs A/C/D before authoring any content.

quality_gaps.gap: Template boilerplate distractor explanations remaining in non-Certified sections of Packs C and D, Sections E and F
quality_gaps.severity_rationale: Blocks certification for the affected items but has zero learner-pool impact (all affected items are non-Certified). Becomes HIGH if certified without remediation.
quality_gaps.pattern: "Option X ... represents a plausible misconception. A candidate may select this option by misapplying a related but distinct concept."
quality_gaps.status: Open — lower priority than QLT-001 and QLT-002. Author during certification wave for these sections.

quality_gaps.gap: 5 non-Certified Section B items with empty distractor ExplanationWrong slots (deferred from DL-025 WAVE 1)
quality_gaps.severity_rationale: Non-Certified items — zero learner impact currently. Blocks certification.
quality_gaps.qids: P1-B-001, P1-B-004, P1-B-006, P1-B-025 + 1 Section D non-Certified (P1-D-070)
quality_gaps.status: Deferred from DL-025 WAVE 1 (2026-07-23 autonomous run). Requires hand-authoring — P1-B-001 and P1-B-025 have additional DL-010 misattribution component.

quality_gaps.gap: Residual empty non-CorrectChoice ExplanationWrong slots in non-Certified sections of Packs C and D
quality_gaps.severity_rationale: All remaining DL-026 items are non-Certified — zero learner impact. Should be resolved during certification wave for these sections.
quality_gaps.status: Open — remediation during certification wave. Certified DL-026 items (Pack D Sections A/B/D, Pack C Sections A/B) remediated in Autonomous Runs.

quality_gaps.gap: 330 case items uniformly labeled Moderate with no cognitive calibration
quality_gaps.severity_rationale: Uniform difficulty prevents adaptive session composition from selecting appropriately challenging case items. Zero learner-facing content defect (content is correct, just mislabeled).
quality_gaps.methodology: Assign genuine difficulty labels based on: (1) Bloom's cognitive level, (2) calculation complexity, (3) exhibit dependency count, (4) distractor deceptiveness, (5) required professional judgment level.
quality_gaps.target_distribution: Easy 15%, Moderate-Easy 20%, Moderate 30%, Difficult 25%, Very Difficult 10% across case pool
quality_gaps.status: Open — recalibration needed pre- or during-case certification

calibration_gaps.gap: Systematic difficulty inflation: ~800-1,000 definition-match items labeled Moderate (score 3) that test at Easy (score 1) cognitive demand
calibration_gaps.severity_rationale: This is the root cause of the Moderate pool being 465 items over target. Practice sessions composed from the current pool over-represent Moderate difficulty, skewing candidate experience away from real exam difficulty distribution. Also masks the true Difficult and VDiff shortfalls — until DL-031 is resolved, recalibration from Moderate→Difficult is a guess.
calibration_gaps.pattern: Stem contains textbook definition of concept X; correct answer is the term for concept X; lexical overlap between stem keywords and correct choice >50%. No application, analysis, or judgment required.
calibration_gaps.methodology: Algorithmic scan: compute Jaccard similarity between stem tokens and correct-answer choice tokens. Items exceeding threshold AND having DifficultyScore ≥ 3 are flagged for human review → recalibrate to Easy (1) or Moderate-Easy (2).

resolving_dl031_enables: True Moderate pool size becomes visible (~300-500 items vs. current 1,226)
Difficult recalibration surface becomes accurate (which Moderate items are genuinely Difficult?)
VDiff and Difficult new-content shortfalls become precise (not 254+550, likely higher after DL-031)

calibration_gaps.status: Open — must be resolved before any Difficulty recalibration or new-content sizing

calibration_gaps.gap: Bloom's misclassification: ~600-800 items labeled Understand that test at Remember level (definition recall, not concept explanation)
calibration_gaps.severity_rationale: Same root cause as DL-031 — template-based labeling without cognitive assessment. Bloated Understand pool (1,276 = 50.2% vs. 15% target) masks the true distribution. After recalibration, the Remember pool will grow and the Understand pool will shrink to something closer to target.
calibration_gaps.pattern: Definition-match items — stem defines a term, correct answer is the term name. Tests recall, not comprehension. Same items as DL-031 (near-perfect overlap between difficulty-inflated and Bloom's-inflated items).
calibration_gaps.synergy: CAL-001 and CAL-002 should be executed together — the same items need both Difficulty and Bloom's recalibration.
calibration_gaps.status: Open — lower priority than CAL-001 because Bloom's labels are not currently used for session composition, unlike Difficulty labels

calibration_gaps.gap: Pack A Section D: zero Difficult items despite 96.2% pack certification rate. ~100 Moderate items are calibration candidates.
calibration_gaps.severity_rationale: Section D (Cost Management) is calculation-heavy — this is precisely where Difficult and VDiff items should concentrate. Complete absence of Difficult items in the most calculation-intensive section is a significant content-quality gap.
calibration_gaps.methodology: Per-item audit of Pack A Section D Moderate items: identify items with multi-step calculations, judgment calls, or exhibit interpretation that warrant Difficult (4) or VDiff (5). Recalibrate upward.
calibration_gaps.note: CAL-003 is blocked by CAL-001 — cannot reliably identify which Moderate items are genuinely Difficult until DL-031 definition-match items are reclassified downward.

calibration_gaps.gap: Moderate pool excess: 1,226 items (48.3%) vs. 30% target of 762 = 464 excess, even before DL-031 reclassification
calibration_gaps.severity_rationale: The Moderate pool is the largest single difficulty tier. Most excess will resolve via DL-031/CAL-001 reclassification to Easy. The residual (post-reclassification) should be evaluated for upward recalibration to Difficult or Moderate-Easy.
calibration_gaps.sub_step: After CAL-001 resolution, audit remaining Moderate items: identify candidates for Moderate-Easy (score 2) vs. Difficult (score 4) based on actual cognitive demand.

calibration_gaps.gap: 330 case items uniformly labeled Moderate across scored_cases2-5
calibration_gaps.severity_rationale: Zero difficulty differentiation in the case pool prevents adaptive session composition. Items within a single case span Easy through VDiff — the uniform labeling is a template artifact, not a reflection of actual cognitive demand.
calibration_gaps.methodology: Per-item difficulty assignment based on: Bloom's level (numeric → Apply=3, select → Analyze=4, multi → Evaluate=5), calculation complexity, exhibit dependencies, and judgment requirements. Case-level difficulty should be within ±1 of mean item difficulty (per CAQS §5.2 CF4).
